title: Mercury Arc — outbound prospecting scrapbook
content:
Top-line: Mercury Arc looks like a mid-market fintech platform (payments reconciliation + merchant analytics) — potentially a strong fit for Redwood Dedicated or Private for two reasons: 1) predictable high throughput for batch reconciliation jobs and 2) data sensitivity (transactional PII) requiring stronger isolation. Below are raw notes, outreach drafts, and an argument map for common objections.

— Quick company snapshot (from public docs + LinkedIn + 1x job post):
- HQ: Denver, CO. 180–250 employees. Series B in 2023.
- Product: payments reconciliation + analytics, integrates with multiple PSPs and accounting systems.
- Infra hints: Kubernetes on AWS, uses Snowflake for analytics, a mention of GPU instances for "ML features" in a 2024 blog post (likely inference offloaded to cloud VMs).
- Potential pain: high egress costs for embeddings search, occasional latency spikes for interactive analyst queries, compliance needs for payments data.

— Key contacts (public + inferred):
- Emily Santos — Head of Data Science (LinkedIn ID: emily-santos). Mentioned ML infra migration in 2024 hiring post.
- Marcus Huang — Head of Platform / CTO (speaks at regional meetups).
- Priya Nair — Product Lead, Analytics.
- SDR/Champion (trial target): Samir Patel — staff data engineer (probable gate for pilots).

— Hypothesis + GTM angle:
1) Quick win: show 3–5x reduction in per-embedding cost for their nightly reconciliation job using Redwood Optimize recommendations (batching + caching + a quantized model variant).
2) Differentiator: offer dedicated enclave (Private) as an option that integrates with their KMS for encryption at rest and audit logs — answers compliance.
3) Long-term: unify their interactive analyst search (low-latency embeddings) and batch model scoring on a single serving platform to simplify ops.

— Outreach sequence (lean, 6 touches, multi-channel) — SUBJECTS / SNIPPETS:
1) Cold email subject ideas:
  - "Cut embedding costs on your nightly reconciliation jobs"
  - "Low-latency embeddings for Mercury Arc analysts — quick idea"
2) Short cold email (for Emily):
  "Emily — saw your note about scaling ML features on LinkedIn. We’ve helped fintechs reduce embedding cost for batch scoring by 3x while keeping analyst search sub-100ms. Thought it might be worth a 15-min sync to run a quick analysis on your nightly job and show potential savings. — Aisha"
3) Follow-up (if no response): 1) case study + 2) short video demo link (30–45s) showing dashboard cost delta.
4) Call script (30 min discovery):
  - Intro (2 min): high-level Redwood value props (unified serving, predictable latency, can run hosted/dedicated/private)
  - Discovery (12 min): what are your SLA targets for analyst queries? How large are nightly batch runs (tokens/requests)? Where does data residency/compliance bite you? Who signs off on a pilot?
  - Quick pitch (8 min): show pilot scope (week-long bench test for nightly job + one analyst route), expected metrics (cost reduction %, p50/p95 latencies), success criteria and data access model (SFTP + redacted sample).
  - Next steps (8 min): assign pilot owner, NDA if needed, tentative pilot dates.

— Pilot proposal (sketch):
- Scope: run their nightly reconciliation scoring on Redwood Dedicated for 7 days with same model weights and a Redwood-optimized quantized variant. Also run a 2-day analyst search latency test (low concurrency).
- Success metrics: >=2.5x cost reduction on batch run OR maintain cost and reduce p95 latency by >30%; analyst search p50 <100ms; no PII exfil detected in logs; stakeholder sign-off.
- Data flow: sample data via SFTP (redacted) or staging DB read-only role; option for Private/VPC if they need no-data-egress.
- Rough pricing anchor: $12k/mo for a small Dedicated pool during pilot (negotiable depending on committed throughput) — purpose: move negotiations away from per-token into committed capacity conversation.

— Objection map (raw rebuttals):
1) "We can self-host; don’t need Redwood."
  - Rebuttal: agree, but highlight ops cost + infra churn. Offer a 2-week bench test comparing total cost of ownership (infra + engineering time). Also cite our Dedicated SLA and managed fallback policies to avoid ops drain.
2) "Data residency / PCI concerns."
  - Rebuttal: Private deployment option with customer-managed VPC and KMS + audit logs. Offer to share our SOC2 report and short architecture diagram for review.
3) "Cost unpredictability with per-token pricing."
  - Rebuttal: propose Reserved capacity with predictable monthly commit and a pilot price that transitions to committed Dedicated capacity if they like results. We can also implement hard quota/cost alerts and token-level cost visibility in Console.
4) "Latency spikes under load."
  - Rebuttal: explain our smart routing + autoscaling profile for Dedicated and show previous latency dashboards from fintech customer case study; propose a canary rollout on one region then expand.

— Competitive signals / intelligence:
- Two competitors in their vendor list: CloudVendorX (simple endpoints) and OpenModelOps (self-host runtime). Mercury Arc values ops simplicity but is sensitive on cost. They previously used an external vendor for a POC and pushed back due to bills. Use that to anchor a cost-focused pilot.

— Email templates (two variants)
A) Short intro for Emily (concise):
  Subject: "Quick idea to lower nightly ML costs"
  Body: "Emily — Aisha from Redwood Inference. Quick note: we helped a payments startup cut embedding cost ~3x on their nightly reconciliation run by applying workload-aware batching and model quantization — no accuracy loss in the rules that matter. If you want I can run a small estimate on a redacted sample — 15 mins to set up. Interested?"

B) Longer note for CTO (Marcus) — focus on infra & pilot terms:
  Subject: "Pilot idea: predictable throughput for reconciliation + analyst search"
  Body: "Marcus — saw your infra notes on scaling ML. Two quick things: we can run a 7-day pilot to compare cost/latency between your current setup and a small Redwood Dedicated pool, and we offer a Private deployment if you need KMS integration. If you’re open, propose a short sync to outline pilot scope and required access. — Aisha"

— Notes to self / open questions:
- Need to validate: nightly job token counts (approx), number of concurrent analyst queries, current embedding model family (open-source vs. vendor).
- Confirm legal/compliance gate: who signs off on Private deployment? Likely Security + Legal. Add to pilot checklist: share SOC2 and KMS architecture.
- Ask Leila for a short case study PDF for payments use-case (was a good match last quarter).

— Quick action checklist (1–2 week cadence):
[ ] Send cold email variant A to Emily (Tue next week)
[ ] Follow up w/video + case study if no response (day 3)
[ ] If positive, schedule 30-min discovery and assign internal owner (Tom)
[ ] Draft pilot SOW outline and pricing anchor (RevOps)
[ ] Prepare SOC2 + architecture diagram for Security review

— Closing note (tone): keep it low-friction. Mercury Arc is mid-market and budget-sensitive. Lead conversations with cost + predictable throughput; ramp to Private talk only after technical/POC wins.

Raw brainstorm ends here — will clean after first response.

–––––
Notes to self (scratch lines):
- Try subject variant: "Reduce ML infra bills for reconciliation jobs"
- If Samir is champion, ask for a redacted sample rather than full DB access (easier ask)
- Remember to log all outreach in Salesforce under Account: Mercury Arc (Account ID TBD)
